params.subhead: What to expect during your first 90 days as a private label client. Week-by-week timeline, key decisions you will make, design milestones, and how to set yourself up for a smooth launch.

params.content:
The clearest, most realistic picture of how your first 90 days will go.

Most private label supplement providers under-explain what onboarding actually looks like. The result is misaligned expectations, surprise delays, and projects that drift past their planned launch window.

This guide walks through the actual cadence of conversations, decisions, deliverables, and approvals you will experience. You will know what to expect every step of the way.

With over 50 years in the health supplement industry, we are one of the most trusted dietary supplement providers. Every private label supplement we provide is doctor-formulated using thoroughly researched ingredients, then scientifically reviewed for efficacy and quality before it ever enters production in U.S. facilities.

When you partner with us, our expert team is with you every step of the way. Help your customers find what they want from a source they trust. You.

items.answer: A week-by-week walkthrough of what to expect during your first 90 days as a private label client. Milestones, decisions you'll need to make, what we need from you when, and how to avoid common delays. Most useful AFTER you've signed an engagement letter.
items.question: What's in the Client Onboarding Guide?

items.answer: After. The Definitive Guide is for evaluation. The Onboarding Guide is for execution. Reading the Onboarding Guide before you've signed isn't bad but it goes into operational detail that won't be relevant until you're actually ready to launch.
items.question: Should I read this before or after I sign?

items.answer: Late decisions on label design and SKU selection. Production has fixed lead times. Design rounds depend on decision-maker availability on your end. The fastest launches happen when one person owns brand decisions and can respond quickly to design revisions.
items.question: What's the most common reason onboarding takes longer than 90 days?

items.answer: No. You need to be available for kickoff, two-three design review rounds (each takes a few days from your end), final label approval, and production go-live confirmation. Total active time on your end is usually under 20 hours across the 90 days.
items.question: Do I need to be available daily during onboarding?

items.answer: We move into ongoing partnership mode. Reorder cycles, future SKU expansion, custom formulation projects, packaging updates. Your account manager remains your primary contact. There's no contract you're locked into; ongoing work is at-will based on what you need.
